rawContent: Some great analysis here from @emi_eaton, @PoliticalOlive, & Angela Carter on the problem & opportunity of #Saskatchewan in the fight to take meaningful action on #climatechange in Canada. https://t.co/OaUGfP9z6P

In the 6th post of the Succession series, Sabine LeBel explains how the Queer Environmental Futures project brings strategies from queer art and activism to #climatechange.
https://t.co/zI2vSswvN7 #envhum

The Arctic is burning. Catastrophic #climatechange dwarfs the pandemic as a global problem.
The changes we've endured with the latter must be used to prepare us for the even bigger changes necessary to grapple with the former. https://t.co/JcsbqZbIY8

In this cross-listed post with @envhistnow, Shelby Brewster considers whether traditional practices of display found in natural history museums can truly be used to combat #climatechange.
https://t.co/c9h4q2SNjI #envhist #envhum

#Saskatchewan finds new ways to delay meaningful action on #climatechange by proposing another technology to save us that has no hope of addressing growing emissions.
Great piece by @DarrinQualman & Glenn Wright. https://t.co/6EVKgsflCm

First it was biofuels (fail), then it was carbon capture & storage (fail), now it's small modular nuclear reactors (science fiction).
The @SaskParty are peddling false promises in the hope they don't have to do anything to address #climatechange.
